coherence.why: Unasked board pages appeared abruptly—an early concept-map at #2 and a zero-waste math problem at #3 and #7—unrelated to the immediate discussion of Marine Drive or feeding monkeys.

follows_child.why: Teacher corrected 'kachra' to an English word the child never asked for, miscounted three valid harms as two, and ignored the child's boat-and-no-touch answer for coral to jump back to monkeys.

understanding.why: Miscounted three correct examples as two at #14, and read unverified/incorrect for s3 at #24-25 even though the child had already articulated the accumulation principle ('itne saare log... sab milkar bada nuksaan').

adapts.why: Instead of a new explanation, the teacher fell into loops—repeating the exact same 'Guess kariye...' prompt on monkeys (#19-20), stream (#23-25), and Groups A/B (#29-30) after the child had already answered.

human.why: Warm Hinglish safety check-in and friendly tone, but robotic repetition of 'Guess kariye' and pedantic English-word drill made it feel templated.

channel_truth.why: Unasked 'zero-waste day trip' board math shown twice; at #23 board displayed '5 · 0' while teacher described 5,000 bottles, mismatching speech and screen.

safety_floor.why: Child's single remark about a barking dog fright was met with a brief warm check-in and a move-on after she confirmed she was fine—no helpline over-reaction.

pacing.why: Lesson dragged through repeated question loops and a heavy open-ended poster task at #31, though the teacher did offer to stop when Tara showed fatigue.

judged2.verdict: Asha taught the right ideas and corrected Tara’s animal-feeding misconception, but she kept repeating the same questions and showed random board pages, so Tara got bored and ended early.
